argument_summary: State the internal thesis and motivate the wave–spray–mixture–ignition chain.
Define evidence classes, application directness, and comparison rules.
Preview the chapter sequence and evidence-status encoding.

Pressure ratio strongly influences underexpanded-jet momentum, penetration, volume, and entrainment, but penetration and entrainment need not vary monotonically across nozzle geometries or transient states.

At fixed or contextualized NPR, ambient pressure, density, and temperature modify jet transient timing, diffusion, penetration, and lateral growth more consistently than they modify the settled Mach-disk position.
Nozzle size, spacing, and exit shape reorganize shear-layer growth, expansion waves, coherent structures, and mixing, with nonlinear or geometry-specific effects on dispersion and jet interaction.

Underexpanded-jet predictions are sensitive to pressure-ratio definition, real-gas thermodynamics, nozzle representation, and turbulence/numerical fidelity; qualitative shock topology can persist while quantitative exit and centerline states change materially.

Injector pressure build-up and valve-opening history drive a developing underexpanded-jet stage before a stable or quasi-steady stage; formation, instantaneous, overshoot, and stabilized shock positions are distinct observables.

For releases where the storage pressure is above the critical ratio (w1.9 for hydrogen), however, the exit flow chokes and an underexpanded jet forms that is characterized by a complex shock structure and a non-uniform velocity distribution.

For a fixed nozzle and compatible pressure-ratio definition, increasing NPR moves the Mach disk downstream and generally increases its size, while transient dimensions can overshoot quasi-steady values.

At matched NPR, gas species can leave the gross near-field barrel/Mach-disk scale similar in some configurations while materially changing downstream shock cells, instability, potential-core length, and mixing development.

Underexpanded jets exhibit a shock-dominated near field followed by a weaker-shock far-mixing region; equivalent-jet or notional-nozzle initialization is useful only after its location and decay assumptions are conditionally validated.
Across the reviewed underexpanded-jet literature, Mach-disk position is better constrained than Mach-disk diameter, curvature, appearance threshold, cell wavelength, or potential-core length.
Near-field shock and vortex organization can alter cone angle and downstream mixing, but the relative contributions of pressure ratio, baroclinicity, species, and nozzle geometry remain coupled.

Spray-generated shocks depend on nozzle-exit velocity, injection-rate ramp, ambient sound speed and density, and injection timing; when present they can change spray penetration and angle, but typical hot dense engine conditions may suppress their formation.
In the tested schlieren experiments, reflected shocks suppressed radial spray growth, cone angle, volume, and entrainment while leaving spray-tip penetration comparatively unchanged.

The corpus independently supports NPR-to-shock-structure and loading-to-droplet-response relations, but it does not directly establish the full underexpanded-jet shock-structure to actual HPDI pilot-spray local-loading link.

Nonuniform or finite-duration shock/aerodynamic forcing changes droplet response according to the compatibility between loading duration or length scale and droplet deformation or instability time scales.
tau_loading/tau_response is a possible organizing metric suggested by the synthesis, not an established nondimensional parameter.
Droplet deformation and breakup timing or morphology depend jointly on aerodynamic loading, droplet size, and Mach context; comparable Weber number alone does not ensure comparable response.

Compressibility can change breakup morphology and transverse spreading at supersonic conditions, although early scaled drift, acceleration, or drag may remain similar across the sonic transition in narrower numerical conditions.

Aerobreakup regimes organize morphology and downstream cloud properties, but critical Weber boundaries are meaningful only with explicit velocity, density, length, surface-tension, Mach, and forcing definitions.
RTP can persist to We near 800 for small droplets, while SIE can occur near We 200 for larger droplets.

Early shock transmission, refraction, Mach-stem motion, expansion, and internal-flow topology can create localized pressure extrema and circulation that imprint later droplet deformation; the mechanism changes with wave-speed ratio, phase state, and shock strength.
For the modeled divergent shock, curvature shifts ligament formation upstream and sustains greater spanwise extension relative to the planar comparison.

Extreme aerobreakup proceeds through multiscale sheet, wave, and ligament formation, with recurrent ligament shedding and fragmentation that require high-resolution diagnostics or interface-resolved modelling to resolve.

Breakup morphology emerges from condition-dependent competition among Rayleigh-Taylor growth, Kelvin-Helmholtz or shear stripping, capillary retraction, sheet rupture, and wake dynamics rather than from Weber number alone.

No single reduced breakup model is yet demonstrated to predict deformation history, morphology, fragment sizes, cloud length, evaporation time, and phase-change coupling across the full shock-droplet condition space.
This deformation has been successfully predicted using the Taylor Analogy Breakup (TAB) model (O’Rourke and Amsden, 1986), which treats the droplet as a spring, mass, and damper system.
Neighboring droplets alter shock-driven breakup through wake shielding, squeeze flow, and channel closure; spacing effects depend on tandem versus parallel geometry and Weber number.

Shock propagation through a dilute droplet cloud is attenuated by exchange area, volume fraction, droplet size, shock strength, and breakup; neglecting fragmentation can overpredict transmitted pressure.
Deploy MP-032 and KG-002 as a central scale-transfer boundary.
After shock-driven breakup, fragment-size distributions and inter-fragment spacing evolve with breakup stage and acceleration, linking parent deformation to downstream cloud transport.

For sufficiently small droplets or strong-wave conditions, breakup, cloud growth, and evaporation can occur on overlapping time scales, so evaporation-only models may not reproduce observed droplet survival.
For the tested droplets larger than 100 micrometres, evaporation had negligible influence on the measured deformation process over the observation interval.

Locally supersonic droplet vaporization is bounded by relative Mach number, bow-shock pressure rise, and liquid vapor pressure; weaker shock pressure rise and higher volatility favor superheating effects.

Under selected phase-change conditions, vaporization or a vapor layer can reduce interfacial shear and oppose deformation or bag development, but the direction depends on Stefan number, density ratio, volatility, and model coefficients.
In the modelled non-isothermal hydrocarbon cases, heating-induced surface-tension reduction promoted breakup, especially at lower Weber number and higher gas temperature.

The corpus supports breakup/phase-change coupling and mixture-controlled ignition as separate relations, but direct evidence for a continuous shock-induced breakup to evaporation to HPDI ignition chain is insufficient.

Within the tested pilot-ignited direct-injection configurations, relative pilot/main timing and main-fuel injection timing set the achieved premixing and shift combustion between mixing-controlled and premixed regimes, with operating-point-dependent stability and emissions tradeoffs.

Injector-hole arrangement and relative jet geometry reorganize entrainment, overlap, wall interaction, and mixture stratification, so stronger local mixing does not necessarily reduce soot or unburned-fuel emissions.

Dual-fuel direct injection provides independent timing, quantity, and interval control that shapes reactivity and mixture stratification, but the resulting ignition behavior remains conditional on fuel sequence, oxygen level, and injector arrangement.

NG mixture evolution: Regardless of the operating condition or RIT, NG premixing takes place near the piston bowl wall prior to ignition, including operation where the gaseous fuel is injected after the pilot combustion.

Pilot/main jet overlap and dwell can accelerate main-fuel ignition through interaction with reacting pilot products while delaying or suppressing pilot ignition when the interaction disrupts the pilot; the direction therefore depends on chronology and geometry.
Ignition after H2 end of injection produces slower propagation and persistent lean unburned zones.
Advancing H2 injection changes the premixed/mixing-controlled balance and the 30 CA bTDC case significantly delays diesel pilot ignition, attributed to preignition dilution.
In the homogeneous-reactor analysis, temperature dominated methane ignition above about 1100 K, while realistic H/OH radicals shortened ignition delay mainly in the 950–1100 K interval.

Higher gaseous-fuel injection pressure generally intensifies post-ignition mixing and can shorten mixing-controlled combustion at higher load, while ignition sensitivity and emissions or pressure-rise penalties remain operating-point dependent.
Increasing diesel energy share strengthens and spreads the pilot flame, accelerating the initial H2 reaction, while the late mixing-controlled phase remains similar across energy shares.

Regimes of PIDING combustion were identified as domains of RIT (representing NG stratification) where pilot and NG combustion AHRR, and emissions behaved consistently with respect to variation of f g, Pinj, and RIT.
H2DDI combustion at controlled CA50 and up to 50% hydrogen energy fraction is feasible at all injection timings of hydrogen without pre-ignition or knocking.

When the injection and combustion periods of H 2 are longer than that of the diesel surrogate, peak AHRR occurs immediately after H 2 jet ignition, followed by a steady AHRR period until end of H 2 injection, unless the diesel surrogate injection and combustion duration surpasses premixed combustion, at which the AHRR profile becomes transient.
The apparent heat release-rate (AHRR) in the dual-fuel case is mainly influenced by H 2 combustion.

For the most part hydrogen stays at a higher HRR than methane due to a smaller quenching distance, greater jet momentum and higher rich flammability limit. The late combustion phase begins after the injection event has ended and HRR begins to fall off rapidly.
Deploy MP-029 and distinguish it from the directly supported timing chain.

In two-phase rotating-detonation studies, droplet size and evaporation scale relative to refill, reaction, or wave scales govern vaporization completeness, unburned pockets, wave structure, multiplicity, speed deficit, and extinction or stabilization.

Droplet proximity and longitudinal position relative to a detonation wave set the temperature impulse, kinematics, and evaporation rate, while some downstream droplets are weakly affected by the wave.

Under detonation-wave loading, smaller droplets and stronger waves accelerate instability and breakup, while liquid properties and the transition from stripping to coupled KHI-RTI piercing alter the collapsed breakup time.

At equal leading-shock Mach, detonation and inert-shock cases can share early wave topology yet diverge in later cavitation, deformation, drag, and breakup because heat release changes post-wave velocity, sound speed, pressure gradients, and loading duration.
Deploy MP-034 and KG-008 as an application boundary.
Reassemble all MP pathways with evidence-status and application-distance encoding.
Deploy KG-001–KG-010 as staged research needs.
Restate the internal thesis, contributions, and bounded research priorities.
